cases.reason: Indianapolis traded Quenton Nelson to Seattle, removing him from the Colts' Week 8 lineup. The official pre-trade Week 8 depth chart listed Dalton Tucker directly behind Nelson at left guard, the current live depth chart keeps Tucker in that reserve slot with the starter slot vacant, and the current roster lists Tucker active. Apply a labelled documented-depth estimate using frozen values; this is not a confirmed starter assignment and does not use market evidence.
cases.reopenOn: Reopen if Indianapolis names a different Week 8 left guard, Dalton Tucker becomes unavailable, or a documented offensive-line role chain displaces another baseline starter.

replacementModel.assumptionRationale: Tucker is the same-position reserve listed directly behind Nelson before the trade and remains the listed reserve after the starter slot became vacant. Treating him as the primary added-duty estimate is narrower than moving existing right guard Jalen Farmer and avoids inventing a displaced baseline role.
replacementModel.baselineRationale: Tucker was listed as Nelson's reserve rather than an existing starter, so the estimate assigns only Nelson's newly vacant left-guard duties and leaves all other baseline offensive-line duties unchanged.

replacements.roleRationale: Current active Colts guard and the listed second left guard immediately before and after Nelson's trade.

closureReview.finding: Nelson is no longer on the Colts roster. Tucker is active and is the documented same-position reserve on both the pre-trade Week 8 chart and the current live chart. Farmer was considered but remains tied to the right-guard depth chain, so using him would require displaced-role reconciliation not supported by current evidence.

cases.reason: Washington placed Terry McLaurin on injured reserve with a season-ending patellar-tendon tear. Official team reporting says Stefon Diggs' workload should not increase, Antonio Williams will receive more targets, and Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown are better suited to McLaurin's vacated spot. Apply a labelled equal-share additional-duty estimate across those three active receivers using frozen values; this is not confirmed workload and does not use market evidence.
cases.reopenOn: Reopen when Washington publishes a Week 8 receiver depth chart, names a primary replacement, provides role-share evidence, or any committee member becomes unavailable.

replacementModel.assumptionRationale: Washington explicitly described a distributed response: Williams gains targets while Burks and Brown are better suited to McLaurin's vacated spot, and Diggs is not expected to take more work. With no supported shares, equal additional-duty weights are the narrow governed estimate.
replacementModel.baselineRationale: The three receivers retain their existing roles and absorb only portions of McLaurin's newly vacant role; no existing starter contribution is removed or reassigned.

replacements.roleRationale: Official team reporting identifies Burks as better suited to McLaurin's vacated spot.
Official team reporting identifies Brown as better suited to McLaurin's vacated spot.
Official team reporting says Williams will receive more targets following McLaurin's injury.

closureReview.finding: McLaurin is on IR and the club describes a distributed replacement plan. Burks, Brown and Williams are the source-supported additional-duty committee; Diggs is explicitly excluded from increased workload, and newly promoted Van Jefferson remains a reopen trigger rather than receiving an unsupported share.
